accessNotes: The landing page only embeds the PDF; the 17-page PDF 'Data Storytelling with an Equity and People-Focused Lens' (September 2024) was downloaded and its text extracted with pypdf; example pages 10, 12, 13 (PDF pages 12, 14, 15) were rendered with ImageMagick. The guide is mostly about equity framing and process, not a formal chart spec: it gives no hex codes, font sizes or axis rules. All colours below were measured from pixels of the example charts (Catalyst purple #3a207d, grey #dedede, orange #f25922 accents), not stated by the guide.
summary: Racial-equity research and advocacy organisation's storytelling guide. Visual guidance is minimal and principle-led: one key point per chart, findings-based people-first titles that name systems as actors, start in grayscale and add a single bold colour (in practice Catalyst deep purple) to emphasise the largest disparity, sort bars meaningfully, and strip gridlines/legends that add no meaning. Examples are clean, sans-serif report and social graphics.

colors.categoricalNotes: No palette defined. Rule: 'Start with a grayscale graph, then use color to emphasize. Less is more with color.' Examples use one deep purple (#3a207d, measured) for highlighted bars and light grey (#dedede, measured) for the rest; a navy/near-black (#070024, measured) single-colour bar chart appears in the RACE COUNTS example. Avoid colours, icons or shapes that reinforce stereotypes; consider colour-blind-visible colours.
colors.notes: Guide document itself uses purple #3a207d for section headings, orange #f25922 for tip lead-ins, and lime #ceea01 annotation callout boxes (all measured). Map example (from a partner report) uses light-to-dark blue choropleth.

axisTitle.placement: omitted; measure stated in subtitle or as a text label inside the plot

source.style: small text below the chart; survey question, notes and 'Catalyst California's calculations based on ...'

typography.notes: No fonts specified. Examples use geometric/grotesque sans serifs (guide body set in Inter-like sans). Plain language, people-first terms (e.g. 'People with Disabilities'), community-preferred labels such as Latinx/Latine.

structure.gridlines: Question them: 'Does it really need grid lines or both axis labels?' Examples keep faint light-grey gridlines parallel to the value axis (vertical for horizontal bars, horizontal for columns).
structure.yAxisTitle: omitted; measure in subtitle or an in-plot text label
structure.unitPlacement: subtitle (e.g. 'Percent of people by race who ...')
structure.notes: 'Only include elements that increase understanding ... go for a clean, minimal look.'

legend.directLabels: Implied; examples label bars by category and use in-plot text.
legend.notes: 'Does every line or shape in a map need a legend?'

marks.bars: Simple bar charts preferred; sorted highest to lowest disparity; one highlight colour on the key bar(s), others grey. Horizontal bars for long race labels; relatively thick bars with small gaps.
marks.notes: Separate multiple points into multiple standalone or connected graphs.

labels.dataLabels: Key findings stated as text next to the chart (e.g. side panel: '5 times more than White people' with the number phrase in bold purple).
labels.notes: Race/ethnicity abbreviations (AIAN, NHPI, SWANA) defined in a note below the chart.

furniture.title: Findings-based, people-first headline that states the one key point and names the system as actor ('law enforcement officers stopped Black drivers', 'SDPD disproportionately targets Black people as gang members'); a smaller bold subtitle states the measure.
furniture.source: Below the chart in small text: survey question with n, notes, abbreviation definitions, then 'Catalyst California's calculations based on ...'.
furniture.other: Social graphics: large headline with the key phrase in bold purple, grey rounded side panel with takeaway text.

annotations: Takeaway text in a light-grey rounded panel beside the chart, key numbers in bold purple. Name data limitations and who is missing from the data.
layout: One key message per visual; static graphics with plain text for social media; interactive charts should offer a static download.
interaction: RACE COUNTS example: interactive chart with a download button to save a static version.
accessibility: Plain language at an accessible reading level; colour-blind-friendly colours; avoid stereotyping colours/icons; people-first, community-preferred labels.

discouraged: complex or novel chart types that wow rather than convey meaning
chartTypes.notes: Use graphs that are easy to read even if commonly used.

distinctiveRules.rule: Start every chart in grayscale and add one bold colour only to the data that carries the message (largest disparity / desired outcome).
distinctiveRules.quote: Start with a grayscale graph, then use color to emphasize. Less is more with color.

distinctiveRules.rule: Highlighted bars in Catalyst deep purple (#3a207d measured), all other bars light grey (#dedede measured).
distinctiveRules.quote: We started with a grayscale and only highlighted important points in purple.

distinctiveRules.rule: One key message per visual; split multiple points into multiple graphs.
distinctiveRules.quote: There should only be one key message per visual.

distinctiveRules.rule: Headline is a findings-based statement in people-first language that names the system as actor, not a topic label.
distinctiveRules.quote: "law enforcement officers stopped Black drivers" as opposed to "Black drivers were stopped."

distinctiveRules.rule: Order bars meaningfully, typically highest to lowest disparity.
distinctiveRules.quote: arrange the racial groups from highest to lowest disparity

distinctiveRules.rule: Remove gridlines, second axis labels and legends unless they add meaning; aim for clean, minimal look.
distinctiveRules.quote: Does it really need grid lines or both axis labels? Does every line or shape in a map need a legend?

distinctiveRules.rule: Below-chart note block lists survey question, sample size, abbreviation definitions and 'Catalyst California's calculations based on ...'.
distinctiveRules.quote: Survey Question: ... (n=...) Catalyst California's calculations based on O.U.R. LA Coalition ...

distinctiveRules.rule: Headline emphasises the key phrase in a heavier weight and the highlight colour (e.g. 'targets Black people' in bold purple).
distinctiveRules.quote: SDPD disproportionately targets Black people as gang members

distinctiveRules.rule: Name data limitations and who is missing from the data alongside the chart.
distinctiveRules.quote: Have we named who the data does not include and where it may fall short

referenceImages.describes: Guide page 12 example from 'Representation in LA City': horizontal bar chart with a large bold black left-aligned two-line findings headline 'BIPOC people do not feel LA City Council takes action on their needs compared to White people.' and a smaller bold subtitle 'Percent of people by race who feel LA City Council does not take action on their needs'. Seven thick deep-purple (#3a207d) bars sorted descending (Black, NHPI, Latinx, Asian, AIAN, Multiracial, White), category labels left in small grey, faint vertical grey gridlines every 5, x axis 0-60 at bottom with no axis title or line, no legend, very light off-white background. Below: tiny grey notes (survey question with n, abbreviation definitions, 'Catalyst California's calculations based on ...'). A lime-green callout box with dashed lime arrow annotates the 'findings-based title'.

Guide page 13 social-media graphic: headline in three lines, 'SDPD disproportionately' in regular black, 'targets Black people' in large bold purple, 'as gang members' regular. Left: rounded light-grey (#dedede) panel with takeaway text, key phrases '5 times more than White people' and 'second highest rate' in bold purple. Right: column chart, first bar (Black) deep purple #3a207d, all other bars light grey, sorted descending, faint horizontal gridlines, small y tick labels 0-40, rotated x labels, measure stated as text inside the plot ('Number of people stopped for field interview cards per 1k people of same race'), abbreviation footnote underneath. Lime callouts explain 'started with a grayscale and only highlighted important points in purple'.

Guide page 10 screenshot of RACE COUNTS interactive chart: findings sentence above the chart, centred title 'Registered Voters (%)', column chart with near-black navy (#070024) bars inside light outlined total-population bars, a 'BEST RATE' grey highlighted band behind the first column, dotted horizontal reference line for the total, faint horizontal gridlines, uppercase small category labels; right sidebar with county name in a dark header bar, KPI numbers on hatched grey bars and 'About this Data' notes; download icon top-right of chart.
